messages:
maria: Quick sync — decision needed on adapter shape for edge routing. We have three goals: tenant-level quota enforcement at the edge, graceful fallback to hosted models when Dedicated is saturated, and clear Console signals for canaries/rollouts. Options: keep HTTP shim (current) or move to grpc-native adapter with an HTTP->gRPC transcoding gateway. Thoughts?

sam_k: I lean grpc between services for perf and typing. But we can’t break browser clients; that’s where the gateway/transcode comes in. Main risk: more moving parts for quota enforcement.

jordan: Hybrid seems pragmatic: grpc internal path, http public gateway that transcodes. Enforce quotas in the ingress (Envoy) via a custom filter so it’s early and observable. Then routing policy can pick fallback model variants.

leo: Quick infra note — if quota is in gateway we need a consistent key for tenant+route to avoid double-counting with batching. Example Envoy local rate limit config snippet: 
```yaml
name: envoy.filters.http.local_ratelimit
typed_config:
  "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.local_ratelimit.v3.LocalRateLimit
  stat_prefix: tenant_rl
  token_bucket:
    max_tokens: 1000
    tokens_per_fill: 1000
    fill_interval: 60s
  filter_enabled:
    runtime_key: local_rate_limit_enabled
  request_headers:
    - header_name: x-tenant-id
      descriptor_key: tenant_id
```
This keeps enforcement fast and observable in Envoy metrics.

pm-alyssa: Product ask — rollout UX: Console needs per-route error %, throttle %, and a one-click fallback toggle for a canary. If a canary crosses thresholds (latency or errors) we should auto-route remaining traffic to fallback variant and surface the reason. Is that feasible?

infra-bot: deploy:edge-gateway v2026.03.15 -> staging succeeded :white_check_mark: (rolling to canary)

sam_k: We also need to think about the batcher + KV cache. If gateway drops requests due to quota, downstream batcher should not treat that as internal failure noise. Suggest adding `X-Quota-Decision: denied|allowed|throttled` header so downstream traces can attribute.

maria: Proposed cutover plan: 1) implement grpc internal adapter + http transcode in gateway, 2) add Envoy quota filter and a header for downstream signals, 3) route 10% traffic to new adapter (canary with console flag), 4) monitor latency, error-rate, and quota hits for 72h, 5) automatic fallback to hosted variant on >=50% error in canary window. Can we build a simple circuit-breaker that routes to hosted fallback when error threshold hit?

jordan: +1. Implementation detail: add header `X-Fallback-Policy: prefer-hosted` and store the canary flag as a route_meta key so the runtime can flip quickly. We'll also need a migration job to backfill quota counters to new keyspace for a few days.

leo: For quota storage: central redis counter per tenant shard. TTL 1h, use `INCRBY` with a Lua script for atomic check-and-consume. Sketch: 
```lua
local k = KEYS[1]
local allowed = tonumber(ARGV[1])
local cur = tonumber(redis.call('GET', k) or '0')
if cur + allowed > tonumber(ARGV[2]) then
  return 0
else
  redis.call('INCRBY', k, allowed)
  return 1
end
```
This keeps the gateway fast and avoids racey quota counts across pods.

pm-alyssa: Also make sure Console exposes per-tenant budget burn and a clickable action: "reassign to Dedicated" (this would auto-open a support flow + suggest commit sizing). That's an important sales motion we want visible during rollout.

maria: Owners: @sam_k implements adapter shim + headers, @leo infra builds quota Lua and Envoy config, @jordan adds route meta and Console signals, @pm-alyssa owns UX and thresholds. I'll draft a short RFC and open a canary run. If no objections I'll kick it off EOW. :thumbsup:

sam_k: ack

jordan: ack

leo: ack — will prototype redis Lua in staging tomorrow

pm-alyssa: thanks all, will write console wireframes and share in #product-design later today

maria: If anyone has strong objections to the hybrid approach speak up now; otherwise RFC incoming.
